engagement_background.objective: Advantia Health engaged Treya Partners to identify and capture hard-dollar cost savings across key direct-and-indirect spend areas, improve procurement processes/controls, and support the private-equity value-creation plan by boosting EBITDA and enterprise value.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Treya will run savings-creation initiatives in 10 spend categories representing roughly $19 M in annual spend (≈$45 M total company spend, $18.98 M addressable). In-scope categories include Employee Benefits, IUD Medical Devices, Diagnostic Devices & Services, Billing Systems/RCM, Medical Supplies, Medical Equipment, Telecom/Data & Voice, Electronic Payment Processing, Data Center/Cloud Hosting, and Office Supplies. Employee Benefits is optional/timed later and some suppliers may become non-addressable after deep-dive validation; all other categories are targeted for completion within a 6-month project window.
constraints_challenges: Limited strategic procurement resources and focus within Advantia prior to the project
Spend data split between two AP/P-card systems (Advantia Mid-Atlantic and Heartland) with incomplete line-item detail, requiring additional supplier data collection
Ongoing integration issues from prior acquisitions leading to fragmented supplier base and contracts
Decentralized, multi-site clinic operations make policy enforcement and supplier consolidation difficult
Aggressive 4-6 month timeline with a minimum $450 K annual savings guarantee
Certain savings depend on behavioral changes (e.g., ordering IUDs in ≥5-unit lots, practice enrollment in vendor programs) or clinical standardization decisions

procurement_environment.data_availability: High-level AP and P-card spend exports are available from two legacy systems; line-item usage and contract files must be requested from suppliers and internal stakeholders.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Supplier names not standardized, limited item-level detail, no centralized contract repository, and gaps remain if suppliers fail to provide data within six weeks.
